strategy.summary: Reproduce PR #62582 on the buggy commit 25607882c53f: build pandas' Cython C parser extension, then run the parser test_ints.py tests that expect integers above 64 bits to come back as Python ints from read_csv(engine='c'). The C-engine cases should fail on the buggy revision because the column comes back as strings, and pass after the fix.

pinned_because: NumPy: no documented constraint and no era ceiling in the evidence; a recent NumPy 2.x is chosen (not evidence-based) because the buggy-era pandas main targets NumPy 2.x
python-dateutil, tzdata: no documented constraint; unpinned, chosen only to satisfy pandas runtime imports
Cython: no documented constraint; unpinned, chosen as the current Cython 3.x since the C parser is compiled from parsers.pyx
Python version: not stated by the evidence (null); use a Python version supported by the buggy-era pandas main, and record the choice
No platform, compiler or sanitiser constraint is stated by the evidence; a standard 64-bit Linux build with a default C compiler is assumed

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/io/parser/common/test_ints.py::test_int64_overflow (conv parametrized, c engine case) and pandas/tests/io/parser/common/test_ints.py::test_outside_int64_uint64_range (val = uint64 max + 1 and int64 min - 1, c engine case)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 25607882c53f, test_int64_overflow[c] and test_outside_int64_uint64_range[c] FAIL: read_csv returns str values (zero-padded for the overflow case, str(val) for the outside-range case) where the test expects Python ints in an object DataFrame, so assert_frame_equal fails. On the fixed revision (the PR head), both C-engine cases PASS because _try_pylong returns Python ints. The python engine cases are xfailed by the PR and pyarrow cases are skipped or xfailed, so they neither pass nor fail the transition. test_outside_int64_uint64_range_follow_str and test_int64_uint64_range are regression guards that pass on both revisions and do not transition.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "from io import StringIO; import pandas as pd; r=pd.read_csv(StringIO('13007854817840017028824'),header=None,engine='c'); print(type(r.iloc[0,0]), r.iloc[0,0])" (buggy: str; fixed: int 13007854817840017028824)

input_output_examples.input: A CSV column containing the integer 13007854817840017028824 (larger than 64 bits), read with read_csv(engine='c')
input_output_examples.buggy_output: The value is returned as a string in an object column (the test's zero-padded form '00013007854817840017028824' is what the buggy path produces for this column)
input_output_examples.expected_output: The value is returned as a Python int 13007854817840017028824 in an object column; the test expects the int 13007854817840017028824 in a DataFrame with column ID

input_output_examples.input: Overflowing big-integer value followed by the string 'abc' (test_outside_int64_uint64_range_follow_str, with the value at uint64 max + 1 or int64 min - 1)
input_output_examples.expected_output: Object column of str(val) and 'abc' as written in the test diff; the PR does not change this expectation, so it is a guard rather than a transition

risks: The defect is in the C parser's overflow fallback, so the C engine must be exercised; the python engine is xfailed by the PR and pyarrow is xfailed or skipped, so only the c parametrization transitions.
The buggy commit must be rebuilt after checkout, because the Cython extension compiled from parsers.pyx is stale otherwise and can make the buggy run look like the fixed one.
The NumPy, Cython, Python and platform versions are not stated by the evidence; the chosen versions are assumptions and could change whether the buggy build compiles at all.

No platform-specific behaviour is evidenced (for example 32-bit, Windows, or sanitiser-only), so the defect is expected to reproduce on standard 64-bit Linux; if it does not, check the compiler and Cython version first.
test_outside_int64_uint64_range_follow_str expects str(val) and 'abc' on both revisions, so it will not transition; a failure there would indicate a regression, not the target bug.
The PR author questioned whether returning Python ints is the desired behaviour, so a reviewer-level expectation may differ from the test diff; the test diff is the authority used here.
The fallback in the except branch passes 0 for na_filter; NA handling is not exercised by the target tests, so it should not affect the transition.

oracle.reference_source: PR #62582 test diff in pandas/tests/io/parser/common/test_ints.py and the whatsnew entry for issue 51295
oracle.why: Integers are compared exactly as Python ints inside an object DataFrame, so no numerical tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 25607882c53f the C engine returns str values for the overflowing column, but the test expects Python ints in an object DataFrame. assert_frame_equal therefore fails on the dtype/value mismatch for test_int64_overflow[c] and test_outside_int64_uint64_range[c].
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR head, _try_pylong converts each overflowing field with PyLong_FromString(word, NULL, 10), so the C-engine cases return Python ints and assert_frame_equal passes for test_int64_overflow[c] and test_outside_int64_uint64_range[c].
